question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Key locations in the Wandiwash campaign of 1760 and their descriptions]
options: Wandiwash Fort — The besieged fortress that was the focal point of the battle
Pondicherry — The French capital from which Lally marched to relieve/attack Wandiwash
Madras — The British headquarters under Eyre Coote from which reinforcements were sent
Gingee (Senji) Fort — The coastal port where the British fleet landed to block the French
wrong_fact: Gingee Fort is a famous hill fortress located deep inland in the Villupuram district, not a coastal port.
explanation: Wandiwash Fort was the central prize of the battle. Lally marched from Pondicherry to besiege it, and Eyre Coote advanced from Madras to relieve it. Gingee Fort was a formidable inland hill fortress under French control, not a coastal port. The British navy operated from Madras and Cuddalore.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Commanders, their forces, and their tactical positions around Wandiwash]
options: Sir Eyre Coote — Positioned the British line of battle in front of Wandiwash suburb
Count de Lally — Entrenched the French forces near the tank and ridge of Wandiwash
Marquis de Bussy — Led the French cavalry flanking maneuver from the western hills of Vellore
Captain Bussy (French) — Captured by the British during the infantry clash on the field
wrong_fact: Marquis de Bussy did not lead a cavalry flanking maneuver from the western hills of Vellore; he was in command of the French infantry on the field of Wandiwash itself, where he was surrounded and captured during the battle.
explanation: At the Battle of Wandiwash, Eyre Coote deployed the British line near the suburb of Wandiwash, and Lally's French forces were entrenched near the ridge and local irrigation tanks. Marquis de Bussy commanded the French infantry line, not a cavalry force from Vellore. He was taken prisoner when the French center collapsed.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Strategic geographical movements immediately preceding and succeeding the Battle of Wandiwash]
options: Lally's diversionary march to Tiruvannamalai — Intended to draw Coote away from Madras
Coote's capture of Wandiwash Fort (1759) — Prompted Lally's counter-march from Pondicherry
French retreat route after defeat — Fled southwestward to Salem and Mysore territory
Post-battle British advance — Coote systematically reduced French forts at Valudavur and Gingee
wrong_fact: After their defeat at Wandiwash, the shattered French forces retreated to the nearby fortress of Gingee and eventually to Pondicherry on the coast, not southwestward to Salem and Mysore.
explanation: Eyre Coote's capture of Wandiwash in late 1759 forced Lally to march from Pondicherry to reclaim it. Following their decisive defeat on January 22, 1760, the French army retreated to Gingee and Pondicherry, where they were eventually blockaded and besieged. They did not retreat towards Salem or Mysore.
